question: The Anacapri chair lift is a vital means of transport to reach Monte Solaro, a place of extraordinary beauty that hosts significant cultural events. However, its single-seat configuration makes it impossible for wheelchair users to use it, preventing them from enjoying this service.

Currently, the lift’s operating rules permits use by two categories of disabled persons, ‘standing’ and ‘blind’, but they do not make any provision for people with ‘sitting’ disabilities, thus denying them the opportunity to use the service.

When it comes to the transport of disabled persons, the Ministry of Infrastructure and Transport distinguishes between facilities that provide local public transport and those that do not. The Anacapri-Monte Solaro chair lift is a vital local means of transport yet it does not seem to be subject to the same accessibility requirements.

In view of Directive (EU) 2019/882 on the accessibility requirements for products and services and Article 6 of Regulation (EU) 2016/424 on cableway installations, I would ask the Commission the following questions: 1.
What measures can be taken to ensure that the Anacapri chair lift is accessible to people with ‘sitting’ disabilities, in accordance with the EU legislation on accessibility?
What actions can be taken to ensure that the Anacapri-Monte Solaro chair lift fulfils the accessibility requirements, given its crucial role in local public transport?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (6.6.

2024) The European Accessibility Act (EAA)1 sets EU-wide functional accessibility requirements for certain products and services, including some elements of air, bus, rail and waterborne passenger transport services, complementing the already existing EU legislation concerning the rights of persons with reduced mobility and with disabilities when travelling by those means of transport2.

In particular, the EAA applies to websites, mobile device-based services, electronic tickets and ticketing, transport service information and interactive self-service terminals3. As such, the scope of the Directive does not cover the physical accessibility of the chairlift of Anacapri.

With respect to Regulation (EU) 2016/4244 on cableways, the latter does not require that all cableway installations must be designed to carry persons with disabilities. Annex II point 6.2 to this Regulation only requires that persons with reduced mobility must be able to use the cableway installation safely if the cableway installation is designed for the transport of such persons.

If it is decided that an installation, not initially designed for the transport of persons with reduced mobility, needs to be adapted to do so, the Member State authorities in charge will have to assess if this implies a major modification of the installation. Major modifications require a new authorisation by the Member State authorities, in accordance with national law, as per Article 9 of the Regulation.
1 Directive (EU) 2019/882 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 17 April 2019 on the accessibility
requirements for products and services, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2019/882/oj OJ L 151, 7.6.2019, p. 70– 115.

2 Regulation (EU) No 181/2011 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 16 February 2011 concerning the rights of passengers in bus and coach transport and amending Regulation (EC) No 2006/2004, Regulation (EC) No 1107/2006 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 5 July 2006 concerning the rights of disabled persons and persons with reduced mobility when travelling by air, Regulation (EU) 2021/782 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 29 April 2021 on rail passengers’ rights and obligations (recast), and Regulation (EU) No 1177/2010 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 24 November 2010 concerning the rights of passengers when travelling by sea and inland waterway and amending Regulation (EC) No 2006/2004.
3 EAA, Art. 2.2(c)). 4 Regulation (EU) 2016/424 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 9 March 2016 on cableway installations and repealing Directive 2000/9/EC, OJ L 81, 31.3.2016, p. 1–50.
